title: Add a callback to call when a config setting is altered
description:
This could potentially help with adding logging / notification logic in downstream product usages of `gcfgenv`

Examples:
- log when an environment variable overwrites a setting
- aggregate and store which environment variables were detected that matched the config struct

title: Clarify README language
description: As the project matures, let's update the README language to make clear the current status

title: Add support for gcfg's struct tags
description:
The `gcfg` format supports renaming struct fields using a `"gcfg"` [struct tag](https://pkg.go.dev/gopkg.in/gcfg.v1#hdr-Data_structure). For example:

```go
type sec1 struct {
	F1 string `gcfg:"another-name"`
}

type config struct {
	Sec1 sec1 `gcfg:"sec2"`
}
```

Given the following input file:

```ini
[sec2]
another-name = value
````

You should end up with

```go
config{
	Sec1: sec1{F1: "value"},
}
```

And similarly, you should be able to set `SEC2_ANOTHER_NAME=value` and have it work with this package.

There is already [a test suite for this feature](https://github.com/rstudio/gcfgenv/blob/main/gcfgenv_test.go#L405-L440), but I never implemented it. But it seems that we use it internally in a few places, so we should probably add support for it. The [`reflect` package supports manipulating struct tags, of course](https://pkg.go.dev/reflect#example-StructTag).

title: Panic overriding a []string field via env var inside a subsection map
description:
# Goal

Fix `setGcfgWithEnvMap`'s subsection-map handling in gcfgenv.go so an
environment variable targeting a `[]string` field inside a `map[string]*struct`
gcfg subsection sets/appends the value instead of panicking.

Two call sites call `reflect.Value.Elem()` on a value whose `Kind()` is already
`Slice` (only `Ptr`/`Interface` support `Elem()`, so this always panics once
that branch is reached):

- the "existing map key" branch:
  `f.Set(reflect.AppendSlice(f.Elem(), newRef))` should be
  `f.Set(reflect.AppendSlice(f, newRef))` -- `f` (`subsec.Field(j)`) is already
  the slice itself.
- the "new subsection created from the env var" branch:
  `f.Elem().Field(j).Set(reflect.AppendSlice(f.Elem().Field(j).Elem(), newRef))`
  needs the same fix, dropping the inner `.Elem()`.

Done when a `[]string` field inside a subsection map (for example
`Flag []string `gcfg:"Flag"`` in a `map[string]*Section`) can be set via its
derived env var, for both an existing file-defined subsection and a
brand-new env-only one, with a regression test for each case.

# Why

A `[]string` field on a plain (non-map) struct section already works: that
code path never calls the extra `.Elem()`. Subsection maps (`[Section "name"]`,
keyed, multiple instances) hit the bug because their equivalent code paths
already dereference a pointer once (`iter.Value().Elem()` / `sec.MapIndex(key)`
gives a `*T`), then incorrectly call `.Elem()` again on the inner slice field.
Any repeatable option added to a subsection map hits a guaranteed startup
panic the moment it's set via an env var, with no workaround except avoiding
env vars for that field entirely.

# References

- gcfgenv.go, `setGcfgWithEnvMap`, the `sec.Kind() == reflect.Map` branch
  (both the existing-key loop and the new-subsection loop)
- Minimal repro (panics on `main`, v0.2.1):

  ```go
  package main

  import (
  	"os"
  	"strings"

  	"github.com/rstudio/gcfgenv"
  )

  type Section struct {
  	Flag []string `gcfg:"Flag"`
  }

  type Config struct {
  	Section map[string]*Section
  }

  func main() {
  	os.Setenv("APP_SECTION_HELLO_FLAG", "beta")
  	cfg := &Config{}
  	_ = gcfgenv.ReadWithEnvInto(strings.NewReader(""), "APP", cfg)
  	// panics: reflect: call of reflect.Value.Elem on slice Value
  }
  ```

title: Capture unknown sections/variables into a dynamic map instead of dropping them
description:
*Problem*

Applications using `gcfgenv` must declare every section and variable statically in Go structs. Some config is only known at runtime — e.g. options for pluggable components whose name and option set come from the component itself, not from the host binary. Today the only way to support that is a fixed wrapper section like `[Component "quartohub"]`; a top-level `[QuartoHub]` section can't be expressed.

`gcfg` already treats unknown sections/variables as non-fatal warnings (`gcfg.FatalOnly(err)`), but the data is thrown away.

*Proposal*

Follow the approach used by `go-ini`: decouple parsing from struct population.

1. Populate the static struct exactly as today (file + env overrides).
2. Collect every section / subsection / variable that didn't match the struct into a dynamic structure instead of discarding it, e.g.:

    type Extra map[string]map[string]map[string][]string // section -> subsection ("" = unnamed) -> variable -> values

Exposed via something like a new `ReadFileWithEnvIntoExtra(cfg any, path, prefix string) (Extra, Report, error)` or an opt-in field on the config struct (e.g. `Extra gcfgenv.Extra` with tag `gcfg:",extra"`) — open to whichever fits the existing API better.

3. Environment variables: decide how `PREFIX_<SECTION>_<VAR>` maps for sections not in the struct. Without a schema there's no way to split section from variable unambiguously, so options include: only allow env overrides for dynamic sections that appear in the file, or let the caller register dynamic section names (and optionally variable names) before reading, so env resolution can use them.

4. Unknown entries captured into `Extra` should no longer appear as `gcfg` warnings (or should be flagged in `Report`) so callers can still detect real typos in static sections.

*Acceptance*

• Static sections behave exactly as before (no breaking changes).
• `[SomeUnknownSection]` and `[SomeUnknownSection "sub"]` contents are returned in the dynamic map, with multi-valued variables preserved.
• Env override behavior for dynamic sections is defined, documented in the README, and tested.

title: A variable with an empty subsection name creates the unnamed subsection beside named ones
description:
A variable with an empty subsection name, such as `CONNECT_LDAP__LOGGING` (two underscores), creates the unnamed subsection even when the section already has named subsections. A bare `CONNECT_LDAP_LOGGING` does not, as of v0.4.1.

## Steps

Read with the prefix `CONNECT` into a config whose map-valued `LDAP` section has only a named subsection, such as `[LDAP "corp"]` in the file or `CONNECT_LDAP_CORP_SERVERADDRESS` in the environment, and set `CONNECT_LDAP__LOGGING=true`.

Expected: no `LDAP[""]` entry, and `CONNECT_LDAP__LOGGING` in `Report.Unused`, as for `CONNECT_LDAP_LOGGING`.

Actual: `LDAP[""]` is created from `Default_LDAP` with `Logging = true`, and the variable is in `Report.Applied`.

## Cause

In `setGcfgWithEnvMap`, the section prefix `CONNECT_LDAP_` is stripped, leaving `_LOGGING`. The second pass ("environment variables that will create new subsections") matches the suffix `_LOGGING`, trims it to the key `""`, and calls `subsection("")`. The `hasNamedSubsection` guard runs only in the third pass, so it never sees this variable.

In Connect, an unnamed `LDAP` entry built from the defaults has no `ServerAddress` and fails LDAP validation at startup. That failure is what the v0.4.1 guard exists to prevent.

## Suggested fix

In the second pass, skip a key that trims to `""`, so the variable is reported as unused. Optionally, also let the third pass accept the `_PROPERTY` form, so that `CONNECT_LDAP__LOGGING` behaves exactly like `CONNECT_LDAP_LOGGING`.

Raised in review of posit-dev/connect#46905.
